context: The operator ruling rejects a UI app with no UX, design or wireframing work at DEFINE. The product owner posture that shapes the gate: it must not be tight, many products need no wireframes at all, some need only a light touch, and the interruption questions matter more than any specific set of wireframes; wireframe richness is better discovery input, never mandated input. A boolean declaration cannot express a light-touch UI without either refusing it for missing wireframes or exempting it from the journey entirely.
decision: The declaration is one of three values, set at intake or by the declare verb, inferred only as a prompt and never as the authority. none: untouched, D0 notApplicable, no discovery file read. light: the journey record must exist and answer the interruption catalogue (each of the six entries covered by an interruption step or ruled out as notApplicable with a reason of at least 20 characters); wireframes are optional and a missing wireframe never fails any check. central: the journey record plus at least one wireframe file per journey step, reviewed at the current content hash. Only a central product is ever refused for a missing wireframe. The catalogue v1 is the six entries from the ux-designer role: lostEmail, closedTab, deadBattery, expiredLink, switchedDevice, lostSignal; adding entries is evidence-gated like the preflight design-shape catalogue.
consequences: A light product pays one declaration and one short journey source. A central product pays the full pack, which is the price the ruling names. The classifier (matchUiSignals) proposes and the person decides, the same precedence src/ui-detection/classifier.js applies to fbs.uiBearing. Lowering the value after declaring needs a recorded reason so a product cannot slip out of the gate silently. The edge-case world the product owner warned about (which wireframes, how many, in what shape) is kept out of the checks by construction: the checks count files and answers, never drawings.

alternativesConsidered.name: Boolean uiBearing
alternativesConsidered.summary: Declare true or false; true requires journey, wireframes per step and review.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Refuses a light-touch UI for missing wireframes or exempts it from the journey; the product owner ruled both wrong.

alternativesConsidered.name: Inference as the authority
alternativesConsidered.summary: Derive the value from UI signals in the brief and the FBS set with no declaration.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The FBS classifier is a keyword scan the operator ratifies; promoting its verdict to a refusal is the known weak point. One declaration is the price of a gate that fails closed.

title: The UI declaration is three-valued (none, light, central) and the gate is proportional: answered, not drawn
